note.explanation: Scientists from different fields can combine their knowledge and skills to investigate problems that are too complex for one field alone. For example, cancer research may involve biologists, geneticists, pharmacologists and statisticians.
examples: The Human Genome Project brought together researchers in molecular biology, genetics, informatics and computer science to sequence and map the human genome.
Climate change research brings together atmospheric science, ecology, economics and sociology.
note.checkAnswer: Oncologists and biologists are two groups of specialists involved in cancer research.
note.simple: A difficult scientific problem can be solved more effectively when specialists from different fields work together.

written.text: Link the study of Biology with that of Physics, Chemistry, Statistics, Geography, Economics and Computer Science.
written.finalAnswer: Biology links with Physics in the study of forces and energy in living organisms; with Chemistry in the study of the chemicals and reactions of life; with Statistics in the analysis of biological data; with Geography in the study of the distribution of organisms; with Economics in the study of the economic use of biological resources; and with Computer Science in the storage and analysis of biological information.

examTips: A long-answer question may ask you to prove that science is collaborative. Give several named examples from the section, and name the disciplines involved in each.
For a question about a particular project, identify the project and state its goal or outcome as well as the disciplines that worked on it.
For full marks, do more than list disciplines: connect each group of fields to its research area, such as climate change research or cancer research.
Use the textbook's examples and exact field names where possible.

solution: Science is collaborative because researchers from different disciplines combine their knowledge and expertise to solve complex problems.
The Human Genome Project aimed to sequence and map the entire human genome and was completed in 2003.
It involved researchers in molecular biology, genetics, informatics and computer science.
Climate change research involves atmospheric science, ecology, economics and sociology.
Cancer research involves specialists such as oncologists, biologists, geneticists, pharmacologists and statisticians.
These examples show scientists from different fields working together on shared problems.

explain.title: What collaboration means in science
explain.body: Science is a collaborative field in which researchers from various disciplines (fields) work together to solve complex problems. Each discipline contributes its own strengths and expertise.

explain.title: Why different fields work together
explain.body: Interdisciplinary teams can tackle problems more efficiently by leveraging the strengths and expertise of each discipline. This often leads to quicker and sustainable solutions.

explain.title: Examples to learn
explain.body: The textbook gives examples from the Human Genome Project, climate change research, medical research, robotics and artificial intelligence, and space exploration. In an exam answer, link each example to the fields involved.

mistakes: Listing a research area without naming the disciplines that collaborate in it.
Mixing up the fields from different examples, such as giving climate change disciplines as the Human Genome Project team.
Saying the Human Genome Project discovered or treated a disease; its stated aim was to sequence and map the entire human genome.
Writing only that scientists work together without giving the examples asked for in the question.
Leaving out important names or writing a field incorrectly, such as confusing computer science with informatics.
